beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: What shape is this?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: A square!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Let's turn it.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Now it's a diamond!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Did turning change any side or corner? It is the same square. We name shapes by their sides and corners.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Start with four straight rods. One, two, three, four. Their ends join to make a closed shape: a quadrilateral.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: This one has no square corners, and all four sides have different lengths.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A square corner fits the corner of a little square, like the corner of a page. This corner does not fit.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Watch the rods move until the corner fits exactly.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Check all four corners. One, two, three, four. Four square corners make this quadrilateral a rectangle.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The little corner marks mean right angles. That is another name for square corners.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Now shorten the long rods until every side has the same length.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Matching tick marks tell us the sides are equal. All four match. A quadrilateral with four equal sides is a rhombus.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: But it kept all four square corners!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Yes. It passes both tests. Four equal sides and four square corners make a square.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Keep every rod the same length, but let the corners lean.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The little square no longer fits. The right angles are gone.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: The ticks still match. So it is a rhombus, but not a square.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Exactly. Equal lengths alone do not make square corners.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Here is a practice question. Choose the most exact name.

do.text: Which is the most exact name?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Four straight sides: quadrilateral. Four right angles: rectangle. Four equal sides: rhombus.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Square tells us both things at once, I see.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: All four names fit. Square is the most exact of these names.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Does this long, slanted shape count as a rectangle?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: No. Its corners do not fit the square.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Its ticks match in two pairs. A rhombus needs all four sides equal. Neither test passes.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: This rectangle looks almost square. Compare a long side with a short side.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: The long side sticks out! Almost equal is not equal. It is a rectangle, but not a square.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A kite also has two pairs of equal sides. These match, and these match. But all four do not match.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: This kite has no square corners either. It is a quadrilateral outside all three special groups.

do.text: Not a rectangle, rhombus, or square.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Can you draw another quadrilateral outside those groups? Draw a short top, two sloping sides, and a longer bottom. Close it up.

do.text: Draw one outside the three groups.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A trapezoid. Four straight sides, no square corners, and the sides are not all equal.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: These are not quadrilaterals. This one has five sides. This one has a curved edge. We need exactly four straight sides, joined closed.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Find the rectangles. Check every shape for four square corners.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: *B* has them. And *D* does too, even though it is a square standing on a corner.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Find the rhombuses: four equal sides.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: *C* and *D*. And only *D* passes both tests, so its most exact name is square.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Which belongs to none of those three groups?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: *A*. But it is still a quadrilateral!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Turn a square, or make the whole shape smaller. Its four sides stay equal, and its four corners stay square.

do.text: Turning and resizing keep the name.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: So it keeps all its names.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: All four are quadrilaterals. A rectangle has square corners. A rhombus has equal sides. A square has both.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Count the sides, check the corners, check the lengths; then name it.
